Hi Michael —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Procurement asked me to collect a short evidence bundle and confirm signer lanes before we request a Private Offer in AWS Marketplace. High-level asks from our side: (1) SOC 2 type II report or summary, (2) a simple network/data flow diagram we can include with our security review, (3) confirmation of who at Redwood signs—legal or an authorized rep—and whether we can do a 12-month term for the pilot-to-enterprise path.

If possible please share an evidence pack and your recommended term/discount for a 12-month pilot (we're budgeting on annual terms but can be flexible). Also attaching our procurement checklist for reference.

Attachment: RFP_requirements.xlsx

Emma —

Appreciate the clear list. Quick answers up front: we can provide a SOC 2 Type II summary and a network/data flow diagram; we typically deliver an evidence pack for marketplace activations that includes the SOC summary, encryption/KMS notes, and onboarding runbook. I'll attach our standard evidence pack and an AWS Private Offer template that legal uses for signatures.

On term/approvals: 12 months is doable; commercial teams often propose a 6-month pilot + automatic renewal to annual on successful activation if you want faster procurement. Larger buys (>$200k ARR) usually require CFO/finance approval on your side — if you expect that threshold, we can prepare a split-approval path in the PO. For discounts we normally price pilot pilots at 15% off list for an initial committed pilot or 10% for a straight annual purchase; I'll flag Naomi to confirm.

Next steps I propose:
- Naomi to confirm final pricing and any Marketplace-specific constraints for a Private Offer.
- I'll upload the Redwood evidence pack and send an AWS Private Offer template to legal.
- If Parkline prefers a 6-month pilot as a path to production, we can draft language in the PO and an ops SLA for the pilot.

Attachments: Redwood_Evidence_Pack_v1.pdf [Attachment stub], AWS_PrivateOffer_Template.docx [Attachment stub]

Thanks —
Michael Grant

Forwarding Parkline's request and Michael's initial reply. Quick internal notes:

- Pricing: for PL-8421 I recommend we propose a 6-month pilot at 18% off list with a pre-agreed uplift if rolled into an annual contract (12% uplift to annual baseline). That helps avoid CFO delay and keeps momentum.
- Marketplace ops: We will need the signed AWS Private Offer (seller-signed) + a Parkline PO to activate. If the deal is under $200k we can route through delegated approvals; over that we need finance signoff.
- Evidence pack: SOC summary + network diagram + data retention policy should be sufficient for their security team to move forward. I've added a quick note for legal to confirm any non-standard terms.

Related links: HubSpot deal https://app.hubspot.com/deal/168293/PL-8421

Thanks Emma and team —

Looping Parkline in here so legal/procurement sees the proposed activation path. A couple operational clarifications from seller ops/legal:

- Signer lane: Redwood executes AWS Marketplace Private Offers via our authorized signing agents. For a pilot, our standard is an authorized business rep (Sales Ops) + a seller-signed PO on the AWS form. For enterprise conversions we'll require a countersign from Redwood legal depending on contract amendments.
- Term recommendation: To keep activation time short, we recommend Parkline request a 6-month pilot Private Offer (with an option to convert to a 12-month term within the PO). This reduces procurement friction and allows seller-ops to activate marketplace entitlements faster.
- Approvals: If the PO value is estimated >$200k, please indicate the buyer-side approver (CFO name or procurement sponsor); that will determine whether we need an expedited legal review.

I've attached a simple signature-flow image to illustrate the routing: seller-sign -> buyer-sign -> AWS activation.

Attachment: signature_flow.png [Attachment stub]

Emma — could you confirm who will sign on Parkline's side and whether Parkline prefers a 6- or 12-month initial pilot? If 6-month, we'll prepare the Private Offer template with the pilot SLA and the discount Naomi suggested.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
